items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Jon Hendricks went crazy over that this morning... he wants me to put it down on paper, and to mail it to him... he wants a very obscure Dizzy Gillespie record... apparently Jon’s got a gig and a record coming up so he needs to hear that.

ctx.x: Well obviously we’re going to have to do another part two or part three here. But I wanted to ask you about a couple of things, and one was your definition of the rhythm section?

Oh yeah. Jon Hendricks went crazy over that this morning here at the IAJE so I now realize that he wants me to put it down on paper, and to mail it to him. But you’re getting a thing. But this is really, you know I was raised by Jo Jones the drummer in the Basie band, and someone we haven’t mentioned yet which is Lawrence Lucie, the rhythm guitarist. He actually goes by Larry but he knows that everyone knows it’s Lawrence Lucie. He just turned 95. And most of this is Lawrence Lucie. It’s a little bit Jo Jones and…
